title: Tariffs: Who Really Pays and Who Really Loses? What the 2018–2019 Data Shows (Fed & NBER)​
summary: Summary of Fed and NBER research on the 2018-2019 tariffs: near-full pass-through to US buyers, net manufacturing job losses, a net welfare loss after revenue, farm bailouts after retaliation, and economists' consensus against tariffs.

assertions.quote: 95 to 100% pass through. You paid, not China.
steel using and export oriented industries lost more jobs than steel and aluminum gained.
We collected money, but we lost more than we collected.

verdicts.note: Fajgelbaum et al. (2020) estimated consumer losses of about 69 billion against 61 billion of revenue plus producer gains, a net loss near 7 billion a year.

assertions.quote: paid farmers over 20 billion between 2018 and 2019 to keep them afloat.

verdicts.note: China's retaliatory tariffs cut US soybean exports sharply in 2018 and the USDA paid about 23 billion dollars in Market Facilitation Program aid in 2018-2019.

assertions.quote: large majorities disagree that terrorists make the average American better off.

verdicts.note: IGM Forum panels in 2018 and 2024 showed large majorities disagreeing that tariffs improve Americans' welfare.

assertions.quote: The terrorists did bring in government revenue about 61 billion. But here's the problem.

verdicts.note: Tariffs raised about 60-80 billion a year in 2018-2019 and over 300 billion in 2025, while pass-through studies show US buyers paid the higher prices.
